result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.contract_nodes_multi()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Contract multiple nodes into a single node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L15230-L15311){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.contract_nodes_multi( nodes, self_loops=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Contract several nodes](/assets/graphs/contract-nodes-multi.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: a six-node graph in two rows with B, E, and F grouped in a tinted region; B, first in the list, is outlined as the survivor and E and F are in the accent color. After: E and F are gone, shown dashed. Their outside edge from D now attaches to B, and the edges inside the group collapse into one self-loop on B." width="100%"} Merges all specified nodes into the first node in the list. All edges incident to any of the contracted nodes are redirected to the first node. Edges between contracted nodes become self-loops (if `self_loops=True`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int | str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs or labels to contract. The first node is the target; all other nodes are merged into it. [self_loops]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), edges between contracted nodes become self-loops. If `False`, such edges are removed. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with all specified nodes contracted into one. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any node does not exist. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node list is empty. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Repeated contraction costs $O(k \cdot E)$ for $k$ nodes: each merge scans the current edge list, and after each merge the graph is one node smaller. The head of the list is the surviving node, inheriting every edge that touched any member of the batch; the remaining nodes disappear along with any labels or attributes they carried. This is the natural building block for community-quotienting workflows where an entire cluster collapses to a single representative before further analysis. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#2325fef8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_path_graph(6) # 1 -- 2 -- 3 -- 4 -- 5 -- 6 result = g.contract_nodes_multi([2, 3, 4]) result.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: This is especially useful for collapsing an entire detected community down to a single representative node: ::: {#80c98ed7 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_path_graph(10) membership = g.cmty_louvain(return_dict=True) community_0 = [n for n, c in membership.items() if c == 0] simplified = g.contract_nodes_multi(community_0) if len(community_0) > 1 else g simplified.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 9 ``` ::: :::
